claims.text: What the strip looks like The PR interval gets progressively longer until a P wave fails to conduct (a dropped QRS), then the cycle repeats.
claims.quote: Progressive PR prolongation until a P fails to conduct

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Rate: bradycardia may or may not be present
claims.quote: Bradycardia may or may not be present.

claims.text: Rhythm: regularly irregular — grouped beats, in P:QRS ratios such as 3:2, 4:3 or 5:4
claims.quote: The Wenckebach pattern tends to repeat in P:QRS groups with ratios of 3:2, 4:3 or 5:4

claims.text: R-R interval: shortens before the dropped beat
claims.quote: R-R interval shortens before the dropped beat

claims.text: P waves: the P-P interval stays relatively constant
claims.quote: The P-P interval remains relatively constant

claims.text: Dropped beat: a P wave that is not conducted (no QRS after it) ends each group
claims.quote: Progressive prolongation of the PR interval culminating in a non-conducted P wave

claims.text: PR interval: lengthens beat by beat — longest just before the dropped beat, shortest just after it
claims.quote: PR interval is longest immediately before dropped beat PR interval is shortest immediately after dropped beat

claims.text: QRS: with a narrow QRS the block is nearly always in the AV node
claims.quote: If the QRS complex is narrow, Mobitz type I second-degree AV block is nearly always in the AV node

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: usually reversible block in the AV node — the nodal cells progressively fatigue until one impulse fails to conduct
claims.quote: Mobitz I is usually due to reversible conduction block at the level of the AV node Malfunctioning AV nodal cells tend to progressively fatigue until they fail to conduct an impulse.

claims.text: Drugs (beta blockers, calcium channel blockers, digoxin, amiodarone), increased vagal tone (e.g., athletes), inferior MI, myocarditis, after cardiac surgery (mitral valve repair, tetralogy of Fallot repair)
claims.quote: Drugs: beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, digoxin, amiodarone Increased vagal tone (e.g. athletes) Inferior MI Myocarditis Following cardiac surgery (mitral valve repair, Tetralogy of Fallot repair)

claims.text: May be physiologic in younger, athletic patients
claims.quote: Mobitz type I second-degree AV block may be physiologic in younger and more athletic patients.

claims.text: Symptoms Usually benign: minimal hemodynamic effect and low risk of progressing to third-degree block
claims.quote: Mobitz I is usually a benign rhythm, causing minimal haemodynamic disturbance and with low risk of progression to third degree heart block
Asymptomatic patients do not require treatment
Symptomatic patients usually respond to atropine
